# The files a dependency's generators add are kept in the build cache as the
# module's overlay, so a module cache that has never fetched it takes them from
# there instead of running the generator again. The shared tier of the build
# cache is what hands one machine's run to every other.

env GOFLAGS=-mod=mod
# -x reaches the generate directives through GOFLAGS, so a generator that runs
# names itself on stderr.
env GOFLAGS=$GOFLAGS' -x'

# The first build leaves the overlay in the build cache, whether it ran the
# generator or found an earlier run's overlay there already.
go build ./...
exists $GOPATH/pkg/mod/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/lang.gen.go

# A module cache that has never seen this module, and the same build cache.
env GOMODCACHE=$WORK/mod2
! exists $WORK/mod2/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/lang.gen.go

# The overlay is applied from the build cache: nothing ran the generator.
go build ./...
! stderr 'gen -out lang.gen.go'
exists $WORK/mod2/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/lang.gen.go
cmp $WORK/mod2/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/lang.gen.go $GOPATH/pkg/mod/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/lang.gen.go

# A file the zip carries is not in the overlay, and it still reads as the zip's.
grep 'the module published this' $WORK/mod2/example.com/generated@v1.0.0/lang/kept.go

-- go.mod --
module example.com/consumer

go 1.16

require example.com/generated v1.0.0
-- use.go --
package use

import "example.com/generated/lang"

var Name = lang.Name()
